newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retailers pledge to buy more in the east.
newsitem.headline: German retailers pledge to buy more in the east.

text.p: Germany's big retail chains pledged in talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Thursday to do more to use suppliers in the former communist east, struggling to find takers despite efforts to modernise their production.
The retailers, including giants Metro, Karstadt and Aldi, promised to double the amount of consumer goods they bought from east German suppliers by 1998, based on end-1995 levels.
In return, the government said it would step up efforts to promote east German-produced consumer goods and help them to find markets both in western Germany and abroad.
Although east Germany accounts for 19 percent of the German population, it produces only seven percent of Germany's consumer goods.

Despite improving production techniques and quality, east German manufacturers, especially in the food sector, have found it hard to challenge established producers who found ready-made markets when western retailers poured into the east after unification in 1990.
In the non-food sector, many manufacturers are still too small to be able to deliver the required quantities.

"With competely revamped product ranges and services, east Germany's consumer goods manufacturers have become equal and competitive partners in the market for the retail sector," said the declaration agreed in talks between Kohl, Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt and the retailers.
"Now it is a question of making use of reserve capacity and possibilities to expand."
